items.title: U.S. Makes Visa Bond Program Permanent — Visas Granted to Targeted Countries Drop 83%
items.summary: Overstays from the targeted countries are down, but so is demand for tourist visas.

items.title: UK Pubs and Clubs Get Tax Cuts. Hotels Get Left Out — Again
items.summary: UK hotels have been excluded from two rounds of government business rates relief. The sector is pushing back, and the numbers show why.

items.title: Mexico Will Spend $115 Million Fighting Rotting Seaweed as Hotels Slash Rates
items.summary: Mexico officials will invest in specialized vessels, offshore barriers and monitoring systems to tackle record-levels of sargassum — but the tourism industry wants more emphasis on environmental solutions.

items.title: Permira-Backed Engine Buys Options Travel to Build Corporate Booking Tool
items.summary: Engine is a startup that spent a decade selling hotel rooms to businesses that never hired a travel management company for help. Now it's just bought a TMC, and plans to build the booking software it thinks all business travelers should use.

items.title: Accor and Treebo Call Off Deal in India: Scoop
items.summary: Accor's 300-hotel target by 2030 was never going to hinge on Treebo alone, but the exit strips out the one partner that gave the joint venture genuine reach into the tier-two and tier-three towns.

items.title: AI Is Deciding Which Hotels Get Considered — Hospitality Revenue Leaders Need a Budget Response
items.summary: AI is pushing hotel discovery earlier in the traveler journey, forcing commercial leaders to rethink who owns visibility, how to measure success, and whether more budget should move upstream before demand reaches traditional booking channels.

items.title: Expedia Acquired AI Trip-Planner Layla: Exclusive
items.summary: Is Layla substantially more advanced that the ever-increasing number of other AI trip-planners out in the wild? Hiring additional tech talent will be a benefit of this deal regardless of whether the Layla platform exists as an independent entity a couple of years from now.

items.title: India’s Inbound Problem: With Its Marketing Budget Gutted, Government Enlists Air India and IndiGo
items.summary: India is compensating for shrinking marketing budgets by giving its airlines a bigger role in selling the country overseas. But this alone won't fix the structural challenges that continue to hold back inbound tourism.
